title: Best Amazon Prime Day tech deals live
text:
Amazon Prime Day — aka Amazon Big Deal Days — is back for October 2026. Buying PC parts, building a new rig, or upgrading your existing rig is getting harder than ever with massive price rises on key components. We're here to find you the best deals to beat the hikes.
Here in our live coverage, you'll find all the best deals curated by our experts in every category, from CPUs and GPUs, RAM and SSDs, laptops and gaming PCs, peripherals, and beyond. We use extensive price tracking and our expertise to bring you deals that are actually worthwhile, accompanied by our extensive benchmarking and hands-on testing data.
Amazon Prime Big Deals Day officially begins on Tuesday, October 6, but there are already great deals to be had. We'll also be bringing you lots of great deals from rival sites that host their own sales during this period, including the likes of Newegg. Remember, Amazon's sale is a Prime exclusive event, so you'll need an Amazon Prime membership to take part. Don't worry, though; even a free trial will get you access.
Quick Links: Amazon Prime Day deals
Amazon Prime Free Trial
Amazon Prime Monthly Plan: $14.99
Amazon Prime Annual Plan: $139
Amazon: All Prime Day deals
Amazon: 73% off computers and accessories deals
Amazon: All Gaming GPU Deals
Amazon: Up to $500 off Gaming Monitors
Amazon: Desktop and gaming PCs
A few of our other dedicated Hub Pages: Best gaming PC deals |  Best RAM deals | Best gaming laptop deals  | Best monitor deals | Best SSD deals | Best PC peripherals deals | Best motherboard deals
Hottest Prime Day Tech Deals
25-Piece Upgraded Electric Screwdriver Kit: was $49.99 now $29.99
Get a 25-piece electric screwdriver for PC maintenance or any DIY task. Comes with a 1,500mAh battery, LED, and extension rod. View Deal
9100 Pro 1TB SSD: was $339.99 now $249
This excellent 9100 Pro SSD gives you Gen 5 speeds of up to 14,700MB/s, but is just $10 more than the slower 990 Pro. A perfect drive to boost your rig's speeds as an upgrade, or the start of a new gaming PC. View Deal
External Power Button for Desktop PC: was $13.99 now $13.29
This slick external power button features a 2-meter (~78 inches) cable and a splitter that lets you connect both to your case's front panel buttons. It also includes adhesive pads and zip-ties.View Deal
Odyssey (G55C) Series QHD 1000R Curved Gaming Monitor: was $329.99 now $189.99
Returning to its lowest-ever price, get a 32-inch curved QHD (2560 x 1440) gaming monitor with a 165Hz refresh rate for just $189, a massive $140 saving. View Deal
October 5, 2026 – 2:38 AM
Well, good morning and welcome to the first day of our Amazon Prime Big Deal Days coverage. We'll be here round the clock to bring you the very best deals from Amazon and rival sales like Newegg, Walmart, and Best Buy. - Stephen Warwick
October 5, 2026 – 2:41 AM
The AI craze has sent the price of many PC components through the roof, so here's a quick state of play. 32GB of RAM now costs at least $400, while a 1TB SSD is now going to set you back at least $150. We've also seen some high price jumps on graphics cards. However, with the right expertise and some good savings, you can still build a PC in 2026; you just have to know where to look! - Stephen Warwick
October 5, 2026 – 3:00 AM
A budget UK laptop
If you're on the hunt for an early deal in the UK this Monday morning, there's currently £200 off this decent Alienware laptop, which would make for a great entry-level or first-time gaming laptop. It comes with a 10-core Intel Raptor Lake CPU, 16GB of DDR5 RAM, RTX 5050 mobile GPU, and a 1920 x 1200 165Hz display.
Alienware 15 Gaming Laptop Da15260-15.3-Inch Wuxga (1920 X 1200) 165hz, Intel® Core 7 Processor (series 2) 240h, 16gb Ddr5 Ram, 512gb Ssd, Nvidia Geforce Rtx 5050 Graphics, Windows 11 Home: was £999 now £799
Get an RTX 5050 laptop with 15GB of DDR5, a 512GB SSD, and an Intel Core 7 240H CPU for just £799. View Deal
Alienware is Dell's gaming arm, a popular and reliable brand for gaming laptops and desktops. This model won't run Cyberpunk 2077 in Ultra settings, but is perfect for some work and play on the go. It would also make a great starter laptop or a gift for someone younger. - Stephen Warwick
October 5, 2026 – 3:30 AM
Secure a MacBook Air for less
Apple's MacBook Air recently got a price hike, like much of the rest of the PC industry. As such, you can no longer buy one for the low of $899 we saw earlier this year. However, this is the cheapest current-gen model going right now. Get $200 off the M5 MacBook Air 13-inch with 16GB of Unified Memory, 512GB SSD, and more.
2026 MacBook Air 13-inch Laptop with M5 chip: was $1299 now $1099
Get $200 off the MacBook Air M5 2026 with a 13-inch display, 16GB of RAM, a 512GB SSD, and Wi-Fi 7. View Deal
Apple's M5 chip features 10-core CPU that is great for on-the-go-computing. This is a perfect laptop for a college student or someone looking to get work done on the go. It will offer excellent battery life, and is extremely easy to carry around thanks to its light weight. - Stephen Warwick
October 5, 2026 – 4:02 AM
UK Nintendo Switch 2 deal
At the start of September, Nintendo Switch 2 prices increased owing to the global shortage of RAM and storage. In the UK, its official price is now £419. This Amazon deal not only gets you a discount off the new price, but it's also a saving on the old price of £395.99.
Switch 2 Console: was £419.99 now £354.99
Save £65 on the Switch 2 with 256GB of memory, with a 1080p screen or up to 4K gaming on a TV when docked. View Deal
The Switch 2 needs no introduction, with exclusive Nintendo titles including Mario Kart World, as well as games like The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. It's a fun family console that can be used both on the go and docked at home on a TV, the latter supporting up to 4K resolution at 60 fps. - Stephen Warwick
October 5, 2026 – 4:34 AM
The cheapest 32GB of RAM you can buy right now
A good 32GB RAM kit (with the desired 6000 MT/s speeds) will set you back a minimum of $437 right now. However, if you don't mind taking it a little slower, this Team T-Force Delta RGB kit is just $389 thanks to this promotion. With 5200 speeds, it's not the snappiest kit out there, but it could be a good solution to securing 32GB of RAM for less in the current market.
T-Force Delta RGB 32GB (2 x 16GB) DDR5 5200: was $459.99 now $389.99
Get $70 off w/ promo code FTTF8296 at checkout. Get 32GB of DDR5 5200 RAM for less- the cheapest 32GB kit currently on the market. View Deal
This is effectively a no-nonsense 32GB of RAM kit that's currently the cheapest on the market in this capacity. It has RGB lighting for a nice aesthetic, and while it won't like up the benchmark charts it's the best budget pick in the current market - Stephen Warwick
October 5, 2026 – 5:02 AM
Another great UK laptop
If you're in the market for a laptop in the UK, this is a pretty cheap price for an RTX 5070 model. The Asus V16 comes with Intel Core 5 210H, 16GB of RAM, and a 512GB SSD.
V16 V3607VH Gaming Laptop: was £1399.99 now £1189.99
Save £210 on this gaming laptop with RTX 5070, 16GB of RAM, and a 512GB SSD. View Deal
Another reasonable beginner laptop that packs a bit more punch thanks to its GPU. It doesn't have a ton of storage but there's enough to get you going. This would be great for someone who wants to do some casual gaming on the go, or indeed a university student who also wants to do a bit of gaming in their downtime. - Stephen Warwick
October 5, 2026 – 5:33 AM
RTX 5090 beast! Save $1,700 on this gaming laptop
If you're looking for a beast of a gaming laptop that will handle anything you throw at it, then this HY HyperX Omen Max could be for you. It's got an RTX 5090 mobile GPU, 64GB of RAM, a 2TB SSD, and a 24-core Intel Arrow Lake processor, specifically the 290HX Plus.
Save a whopping $1,700 on this HyperX Omen Max 16-inch laptop. Comes with a 240Hz display, RTX 5090 GPU, 64GB of DDR5 RAM, a 2TB SSD, and Wi-Fi 7. View Deal
With its enormous CPU and a 24GB VRAM 5090, this laptop will handle any gaming title you can throw at it in its native 2560 x 1600 resolution. It also has a ton of storage for games and files, as well as 64GB of RAM for multitasking. This is a futureproof laptop that doesn't need any upgrades, and right now it's got a huge discount that makes it cheaper than the 32GB, 1TB version. - Stephen Warwick
October 5, 2026 – 5:59 AM
You can snag a 240 Hz OLED gaming monitor at Walmart for just $269 — 2560 Acer Nitro with QD panel is $81 off
(Image credit: Acer / Walmart)
So many things in the PC space (and pretty much everywhere else) are more expensive these days. But the price of OLED monitors continues to decline, as evidenced by this 27-inch, 240 Hz model (VG277U Xbiip) from Acer's Nitro line. It sports a 240 Hz QD-OLED panel rated at 400 Nits of brightness and a 0.03 ms response time. That's a lot of monitor for the current Walmart asking price of $269.
VG277U Xbiip: was $349 now $269
This mid-sized gaming monitor sports a QD-OLED panel rated at a decent 400 nits of brightness, with a 240 Hz refresh and a resolution of 2560 x 1440. If you're after a gaming screen on a budget and want inky blacks and saturated colors, this is a tough deal to beat.View Deal
We haven't tested this monitor, so we can't vouch for its performance. But Acer typically makes solid gaming screens, and the QD-OLED panel ensures that the blacks will be truly black, and colors should be vivid. The 400-nit brightness rating isn't the best for an OLED, but it should be more than sufficient, unless you like to game in a bright sunlit room.
The VG277U Xbiip has one DisplayPort (1.4) and two HDMI (2.1) ports. The bezels are also barely there, save for a small lip at the bottom. And of course, AMD FreeSync Premium is supported, and you should see smooth performance gaming with an Nvidia card as well. - Matthew Safford
October 5, 2026 – 6:35 AM
Dell's excellent XPS 13 now starts at just $599 at Best Buy — 16GB model is just $799
(Image credit: Tom's Hardware)
Dell's XPS 13 is one of the best MacBook Neo alternatives for those who prefer Windows. And now, thanks to Best Buy's Techtober sale, you can snag the 8GB model for just $599 ($100 less than the Neo), or double the RAM to 16GB for just $799. That's $200 less than the current price direct from Dell, and a steal if you're in need of a slim and light laptop for mainstream productivity tasks.
XPS 13 (2026): was $799 now $599
This model of the XPS 13 sports a Wildcat Lake Intel Series 3 Core 5 320 CPU, 8GB of RAM, 512GB of storage, and a 13.4-inch, 2560 x 1600 touchscreen. It weighs just 2.2 pounds. View Deal
XPS 13 (2026): was $999 now $799
This model of the XPS 13 sports a Wildcat Lake Intel Series 3 Core 5 320 CPU, 16GB of RAM, 512GB of storage, and a 13.4-inch, 2560 x 1600 touchscreen. It weighs just 2.2 pounds. View Deal
When we tested Dell's latest XPS 13, we found it to have a pleasing premium build, excellent speakers for its size, and to be free of bloatware. Performance was also in line with other Wildcat Lake laptops, which makes it fine for basic productivity tasks, but not great for anything too demanding.
The standout feature in our tests, though, was battery life.
(Image credit: Tom's Hardware)
At between 14 and 15 hours in our battery test, the XPS 13 beat the MacBook Neo in unplugged longevity by about an hour or more, making it a good laptop if you need to work away from a power plug. It's screen is also no slouch, testing near 400 nits, while being about as colorful as the panel in the MacBook Neo. - Matthew Safford
October 5, 2026 – 7:00 AM
Corsair's 1000W, modular ATX 3.1 RM1000e power supply hits $109 at Best Buy — lowest-ever price for this beefy PSU with ThermaProtect
(Image credit: Tom's Hardware)
High-wattage power supplies rarely come cheap, especially from well-established brands like Corsair, but Best Buy is offering up the fully modular RM1000e for just $109, which seems to be a record-low price. The ATX 3.1 PSU is Cybenetics Platinum rated, has a zero RPM mode so it will be silent much of the time, and features Corsair's ThermalProtect 12V-2x6 Cable with Over Temperature Protection (OTB) to (hopefully) keep your precious high-priced GPU from melting down in your expensive rig.
RM1000e: was $179.99 now $109.99
This fully modular ATX 3.1 power supply is rated to 1000 watts, is Platinum rated for efficieny, and comes with a 12V-2x6 cable that features ThermalProtect to monitor for unsafe cable temperatures. View Deal
When we reviewed the RM1000e last year, we praised it for its "tight voltage regulation, excellent ripple suppression, and stable thermal management." It also has a 7-year warranty and ran quietly under typical conditions.
The PSU does use some mid-tier components and doesn't come with a generous amount of accessories, but at this low price that's much easier to accept than when we tested it at $170.
October 5, 2026 – 7:31 AM
Team Group's 4TB T-Force G50 EVO SSD drops below 10 cents per gigabyte — PCIe 4.0
Thanks to ongoing demand from AI hyperscalers, real SSD deals have been hard to come by for nearly a year now. But Newegg is offering Team Group's 4TB G50 EVO M.2 SSD for $455.99, with a $70 coupon code (APC852) that takes it down to $385.99. That's easily the best price ever for this relatively recent model, and takes the pricing to about 9.4 cents per gigabyte.
T-Force G50 Evo (4TB): was $495.99 now $385.99
Promo code: APC852
This DRAMless PCIe 4.0 SSD is rated to 5,000 MB/s reads and 4,700 MB/s writes, and 1200TBW. It uses 3D QLC NAND, and has a 3-year warranty.View Deal
The Evo model of the G50 looks to have only come onto the market in the last month, and we haven't tested it. So it's tough to drill into details about its performance beyond its model's 5,000 / 4,700 read/write rating. But it's likely a better fit as a secondary drive for games and media than as a boot drive if you're after the snappiest performance.
Still, I've had good experience with Team Group's budget drives in the past. I've been using a 4TB MP44 drive for game storage in my main rig for years and have had zero complaints.  - Matthew Safford
October 5, 2026 – 7:58 AM
Creative's excellent Pebble Pro speakers hit their lowest price since early 2025  — compact 30W USB-C, Bluetooth speakers drop to $59
Creative's Pebble Pros have long been on our list of the best PC speakers for their compact, angled, attractive design and their ability to run solely over USB-C. But their price has crept up over the past couple of years (just like basically everything), making them less of a value play. But now at Amazon, they are back down to $59.99, a price we haven't seen since mid-April of 2025.  Considering they've spent most of 2026 at around $75, that makes this a sweet deal if you're looking for a simple, good-sounding desk audio setup.
Pebble Pro: was $69.99 now $59.99
A 14% savings might not seem like much, but these excellent compact speakers have been selling for about $5 above list price for most of 2026. They performed well in our testing and can hit 30W RMS/60W peak, though you'll have to bring your own 30W PD power adapter to get the loudest sound output.View Deal
In our review, we found the Pebble Pros a big step up in sound and bass over the previous-gen Pebble V3s. The speakers are permanently connected to each other, but the cable is an ample six feet long. The drivers are nicely angled up toward your ears, so you don't have to think about speaker stands, and connectivity includes USB-C for data, USB-C PD for power, and a 3.5 mm aux jack. There are also a pair of 3.5 mm jacks on the side of the right speaker for a headset and a mic.
As touched on earlier, you'll need a separate 30W USB power adapter to get the maximum sound output. If you solely draw power via a USB-C connector, the output will be limited to 10W.  - Stephen Warwick
October 5, 2026 – 8:28 AM
This 1440p, 27-inch LG gaming monitor is a steal for under $150
While the Big Deal Days haven't technically started, Amazon's deals right now include this LG curved gaming monitor for just $149.99. The 27-inch LG 27GS60QC-B Ultragear is a good option on a budget and, for less than $150, easily rivals the competition at this price point.
The UltraGear 27GS60QC-B is a 27-inch monitor with a 1440p resolution, 180Hz refresh rate, and 1ms GtG response time. It uses a VA panel and comes with FreeSync support. View Deal
You're getting a 27-inch display there with a 1440p resolution, so this is a good upgrade to consider if you're still rocking a 1080p display. It has a 180Hz refresh rate, along with a 1ms GtG response time. It's a VA panel, so you can expect higher contrast and deeper blacks than IPS rivals, and it comes with AMD FreeSync support to eliminate screen tearing completely. - Ben Stockton
October 5, 2026 – 9:11 AM
Powerolwl's AA Lithium rechargeable batteries are great for high-drain devices, and you can get eight, plus a charger for $25 ahead of Prime Day
Panasonic's Eneloops have been the gold standard of rechargeable batteries for several years, but they're also expensive. I've had a very good experience with the Powerowl brand, and after shifting to the company's lithium AAs early this year, I'm never going back, at least when it comes to high-gain devices. Today at Amazon, you can grab eight AA, 3600 mWh AA Powerowl cells, plus a USB-C charger, for just $24.99. That's $15 less than the comparable Philips cells. And of the three sets I own, I have had exactly one battery die on me since February.
1.5V Rechargeable Lithium AA Batteries 8 Pack with Charger: was $29.99 now $24.99
These lithium rechargables excel in high-gain devices and are rated to 3600 mWh. They include a charger with a USB-C port (no USB-C charger is included, but you probably own a few), and I've found them to last much longer than NiMH in devices like door locks.View Deal
I've found these batteries to be a game-changer for my smart door locks, with the Lithium cells lasting at least twice as long as the NiMH cells I've used for years. They worked so well that after I bought the first set and used them once, I bought two more.
Out of the 24 batteries that are now in heavy rotation powering my devices since February, I did encounter one cell that stopped working after the first or second charge, which is annoying. But the 23 others are working as expected (or better than expected, really), running my locks for months at a time without complaint.
October 5, 2026 – 9:30 AM
Rosewill's M.2 SSD cloner is super useful, now just $37 with promo code
(Image credit: Tom's Hardware)
You might not need it right now, but when you need to clone a drive, an M.2 SSD cloner can be a life-saver. And right now, the Rosewill model I own is on sale $12 off, or $37 with promo code FTTF7766 Newegg. It works with NVMe M.2 SSDs (sorry SATA), and can clone a drive either offline, or via software, with a 20 Gbps interface.
NVMe SSD Cloner: was $59.99 now $37.99
$12 off w/ promo code FTTF7766
With support for NVMe M.2 SSDs and offline cloning, this handy device makes it simple to move your files or OS from one drive to another. And with a 20 Gbps USB-C interface, it's also speedy in your OS of choice if you want to use software to clone or move your data between drives.View Deal
Using the cloner is pretty straightforward. You plug in the included USB-C power adapter, put your source drive in the left slot, the destination drive in the right slot, press the power button on the back, and a few logos light up, letting you know you're ready to go. Press the clone button on the top, and drive cloning will commence (provided your destination is the same size or larger than your source).
But you can also use it with your own software, which you'll likely have to do if the drives you are cloning to/from aren't the same size. It can make a complex drive cloning task take just a few minutes, and it's also handy to have if you just need to plug in an old drive to see what, if any, files are on it. - Matthew Safford
October 5, 2026 – 9:59 AM
Get Logitech's G Pro X Superlight 2 for a super-light price of $69
(Image credit: Tom's Hardware)
Logitech's award-winning ultra-light pseudo-ambidextrous wireless gaming mouse weighs just 2.12 ounces (60g) and sports the brand's Hero 2 optical sensor. And it's currently on sale for the lowest price we've seen it at: $69 at Walmart.
G Pro X Superlight 2: was $179.99 now $69
Logitech's ultralight 60g wireless mouse features a pseudo-ambidextrous symmetrical shape and sports the brand's Hero 2 optical sensor and Lightforce hybrid optical/mechanical switches. View DealTom's HardwareTom's HardwareTom's HardwareTom's Hardware
The G Pro X Superlight 2 has a maximum sensitivity of 32,000 DPI and a maximum speed of 500 IPS and can handle up to 40 G's of force. It has a lightweight plastic shell with a smooth, soft-touch finish, and five programmable buttons. The primary buttons feature Logitech's Lightforce hybrid mechanical/optical switches, which are tactile and clicky (and somewhat loud). You can read my full review of the Logitech G Pro X Superlight 2 here. — Sarah
October 5, 2026 – 10:46 AM
Plug in all your USB things with this 11-port powered hub, on sale for $42 – premium hub sports two USB-C data ports, 20W charging port, and seven USB-A
If you’re like me, you’re always running out of USB ports. But I’ve found this powered ikuai hub to be a great solution. It has a 20W charging port on the end and 10 data ports, three of which are 10 Gbps. For those concerned about power draw (or just the peripheral clutter of keeping a bunch of devices connected to your system at all times), it has individual buttons on the side for switching off the ports you aren’t using. It also has a premium metal frame, and is currently on sale at Amazon for $42.49.
11-in-1 Hybrid USB Hub: was $49.98 now $42.49
With 11 ports and up to 10 Gbps speed, a solid aluminum shell, and buttons so you can cut the power to individual ports, this USB hub is a great addition to your desk. It has external power for better stability, and even a 20W USB-C PD port on the end for charging phones or peripherals.View Deal
The sole thing to keep in mind about this (and basically any) hub, is that it has a single 10 Gbps input. So don't expect to plug in multiple high-data devices (like SSDs) and have them run simultaneously at full speed. If that's what you need, you should get a Thunderbolt or USB4 hub, though you'll typically need to spend significantly more.
October 5, 2026 – 11:06 AM
Acer Nitro MGA270U gaming monitor plummets to just $135 — 27 inches of 200 Hz 1440p gaming goodness
Do GPU, memory, and CPU prices have you feeling down? Well, not every segment of the PC gaming space has been hit with catastrophic price hikes, particularly when it comes to gaming monitors. In fact, gaming monitors have increasingly become more affordable, as maturing OLED technology pushes VA and IPS panels even lower. For instance, take a look at the Acer Nitro MGA270U X2biipx. This monitor has a typical MSRP of $229.99, but Walmart is currently selling the monitor for just $135, representing a $94.99 discount.
The Acer Nitro MGA270U is a great, entry-level 1440p gaming monitor featuring a 27-inch IPS panel. THe Nitro MGA270U has a maximum refresh rate of 200 Hz, and fully supports AMD FreeSync Premium.View Deal
And we're not talking about a staid 144 Hz 1080p panel either; the MGA270U features a 1440p (WQHD) IPS panel with a 200 Hz native refresh rate (AMD FreeSync Premium Pro supported). Acer also gives the monitor its Zero Frame design with an anti-glare finish, which features minimal bezels around the top and sides, and a slightly larger "chin" at the bottom.
Typical brightness is listed at 250 nits, and you'll find two HDMI 2.1 and one DisplayPort 1.4 port onboard.
So if your wallet has been feeling the sting of the AI revolution, treat yourself to this sub-$150 value buy if you're looking to maximize your tech dollars. — Brandon Hill
October 5, 2026 – 11:49 AM
Amazon disounts its flagship Eero Max 7 Wi-Fi 7 mesh routers by 30%
(Image credit: Amazon)
It’s hard to believe that it’s been almost three years since we first took a look at the Amazon Eero Max 7, as it was one of the very first Wi-Fi 7 routers to hit the market. As such, it gave us a glimpse of the speed improvement that would be fleshed out as more Wi-Fi 7 devices hit the market. Given that the Eero Max 7 now has some age on it, Amazon is offering a pretty generous discount, taking 30 percent off configurations.
The Eero Max 7 is Amazon's flagship Wi-Fi 7 mesh router system. This is a 2-pack, with each node featuring two 2.5 GbE ports and two 10 GbE ports.View Deal
That means that you can get the Eero Max 7 2-pack for just 799.99, compared to its usual asking price of $1,149.99.
The Eero Max 7 is a tri-band Wi-Fi 7 mesh router with a 2x2 2.4 GHz band (688 Mbps), a 4x4 5 GHz band (8,647 Mbps), and a 4x4 6 GHz band (11,530 Mbps). The four satellites can communicate via a dedicated wireless backhaul or a wired backhaul for improved performance. With this two-pack, you’ll get up to $5,000 square feet of coverage. — Brandon Hill
October 5, 2026 – 12:20 PM
Save $70 on the MSI MPG X870E Gaming Plus Wifi motherboard – All-time low price of $169 makes this mid-range board a great option to upgrade or start your AM5 build today
Although we’re all neck-deep in the AIpocalypse, some items, like motherboards, haven’t seen prices skyrocket and become unaffordable like RAM, video cards, and storage. In fact, we see quite a few deals on individual boards (read: not in a combo deal with multiple items), and we found a gem in the MSI X870E Gaming Plus Wifi for only $170 ($70 off) with promo code FTT8257. This motherboard, although we didn’t personally review it, is a quality budget X870E solution that supports current and next-gen AM5-based processors and is a solid base for building your new system. Or at this price, a worthwhile upgrade from X670, offering more and faster ports (think more M.2, more USB, etc.), an updated appearance, and native support for 9000 series processors like the Ryzen 7 9800X3D ($429 and includes two freebies) or 9850X3D at $469 that’s also currently on sale.
(Image credit: Future)
Matching it's ALL-TIME LOW, the MSI X870E Gaming Plus Wifi is a solid budget-class motherboard on the X870E platform.View Deal
The MSI X870E Gaming Plus Wifi offers users plenty of USB ports on the rear IO, including USB4 (40 Gbps) Type-C, three M.2 connectors (one PCIe 5.0), and four SATA ports for storage, fast networking with 2.5 GbE and Wi-fi 7 (the faster 320Hz version, even), and a black appearance with white highlights that will blend in with most any dark/black build theme. It doesn’t include any RGB bling, but it has plenty of integrated headers to add them if needed.
At only $170 (and $70 off with the promo code) for the X870E Gaming Plus Wifi, this is one of the best standalone deals for a budget X870E motherboard. In fact, it’s one of the least expensive options out there that isn’t an open box. You can probably find X870 or B850 options for less, but you may run into lane sharing with M.2 drives since those platforms offer less available bandwidth from the chipset.
October 5, 2026 – 12:55 PM
Acer's Predator XB273U F5 27-inch 1440p 200 Hz gaming monitor gets a massive $220 discount
(Image credit: Acer)
We have another Acer monitor deal coming in hot, this time from Amazon. The Acer Predator XB273U F5 monitor is currently listed at $545.01 from the online retail giant, but a $220.89 instant coupon (available on the product page) drops the price to just $324.12. The price on the XB273U F5 has ranged from $539.39 to $546.27 according to Amazon's own price checker tool, so this is a killer deal that shouldn't be ignored.
The Acer Predator XB273U F5 is a fantastic 27-inch 1440p 200 Hz gaming monitor supporting Nvidia G-Sync Pulsar tech.View Deal
We reviewed the XB273U F5 earlier this year, and it's a 27-inch IPS monitor with a 2560 x 1440 resolution and a 360 Hz native refresh rate. The panel supports AMD FreeSync Premium, and it's also one of the first monitors that we tested that supports Nvidia's G-Sync Pulsar technology. G-Sync Pulsar helps to further smooth motion without contributing to a reduction in overall screen brightness.
Our gaming monitor reviewer, Christian Eberle, described the monitor, writing, "Based on the smoothness I observed and its super low input lag, the XB273U F5 is the first LCD that delivers gaming performance equal to a premium OLED gaming monitor. G-Sync Pulsar provides visually perfect motion resolution and instant control response at 360 Hz."
When it comes to ports, you'll find two HDMI 2.1 ports, one DisplayPort 1.4, and an onboard USB hub (three downstream). — Brandon Hill
October 5, 2026 – 1:26 PM
13-inch MacBook Air with M5 falls to its original $1,099 starting price
(Image credit: Tom's Hardware)
Remember when, just a few months ago, the cost of memory hadn't led Apple to increase the price of its Macs? Well, for a brief moment during the sales surrounding Prime Day, you can relive those days. The 13-inch MacBook Air with M5, Apple's premium, thin-and-light laptop, is back down to $1,099 at Best Buy and Amazon.
MacBook Air (13-inch, M5): was $1299 now $1099
The MacBook Air with M5, 16GB of memory, and 512GB of RAM is down to $1,099, a great deal for Apple's most high-end, ultraportable notebook. The sale covers all four colors.View Deal
